item.title: Python: Differentiating In-Place Addition (+=) from Standard Addition (+) Operations
item.description:
“Python: Differentiating In-Place Addition (+=) from Standard Addition (+) Operations”

When working with object manipulation in Python, the choice between using the augmented assignment operator (+=) and the standard addition operator (+ followed by assignment) can lead to profoundly different results, particularly concerning object mutation. How does Python decide which internal method to call, and what are the practical implications for mutable types like lists versus immutable types like integers?
